a: Redis types include strings, lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes, streams, and bitmaps.
TTL expires keys after a time-to-live; used for caches and sessions.
PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE delivers messages to channels for lightweight fan-out.
Streams are append-only logs with consumer groups for reliable messaging.
Pipelining batches commands to reduce round-trips.
Redis Cluster shards data across nodes for scale and availability.
RDB snapshots and AOF logs provide durability options.
Lua scripts run atomically on the server for complex operations.
INCR + EXPIRE patterns implement fixed-window rate limits.
Prevent stampedes with locks, probabilistic early expiry, or single-flight.
